name: Joshua
overview: Joshua was a male figure noted in Scripture as the governor of Beersheba, according to 2 Kings 23:8. While his tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not recorded, his role as a leader in this capacity is acknowledged. There are no further notes provided about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Joshua means 'YHWH saves,' highlighting a divine aspect to his identity. This proper name, referenced in 2 Kings 23:8, reflects the saving power of the Lord but was not specifically given by God in this instance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for this Joshua beyond what is noted in his unique attribute as governor of Beersheba. There are no listed connections or relatives in the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Joshua's significance in the biblical narrative is primarily tied to his administrative role in Beersheba, as mentioned in 2 Kings 23:8. Although the prior references to Joshua as Moses' successor and leader of Israel into the Promised Land are noted, this particular individual is distinguished by his governance. His name's meaning points to the Lord's saving power, which aligns with the broader biblical theme of God’s deliverance through His appointed leaders.
